reason: 'Keep all these things sacred which I have kept, even as I have kept them.' A five-word run, and the machine's best offer for the verse. The verb decides against it. John 15:10's keeping is obedience — 'even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love' — and Alma's is custody: the object of the verb is a set of plates, and the whole paragraph is about who physically holds them and hands them on. The same run has already been declined at 1 Nephi 2:20 and 2 Nephi 4:4, where it attached to the prosperity conditional; here it attaches to an inventory. The register keeps the row because 'keep the commandments' is genuinely a live idiom two verses later at 37:13, and a reader who saw the run at 37:2 could reasonably think John was in the room.

sharedText: his paths are straight; and his course is one eternal round
reason: The Book of Mormon's formula for divine immutability, and it has one adjudication in this book, at Alma 7:20, where the same speaker sets 'he cannot walk in crooked paths', 'neither doth he vary from that which he hath said', and 'his course is one eternal round' against James 1:17's 'no variableness, neither shadow of turning'. Alma 37:12 is the compressed form of that same sentence — straight paths, one eternal round — thirty chapters later in Alma's own mouth, and it is his formula recurring rather than a fresh borrowing (ADJUDICATING §4). Its first statement in the corpus is 1 Nephi 10:19. A reader tempted by Isaiah 40:3 or Matthew 3:3 ('make his paths straight') should note that the straightness there is a road to be prepared by men, not a property of God's own course.

sharedText: if ye will keep my commandments, ye shall prosper in the land
reason: The land covenant in its fullest Book of Mormon form, given here as direct divine speech with both halves intact — 'if ye will keep my commandments, ye shall prosper in the land; but if ye keep not his commandments, ye shall be cut off from his presence.' Its adjudication is at 1 Nephi 2:20, to 1 Kings 2:3, where the promise is first stated; within Alma the recurrence is registered at Alma 36:1, whose chiasm turns on it. Nothing at 37:13 departs from the established formula, so the row here is a cross-reference rather than a link. Note that the negative clause reads 'cut off from HIS presence' where 1 Nephi 2:21 has 'the presence of the Lord' and 2 Nephi 4:4 has 'my presence' — the drift in the possessive is catalogued at 2 Nephi 4:4.

sharedText: the blood of those which they murdered, did cry unto the Lord
reason: 'They murdered all the prophets of the Lord which came among them … and the blood of those which they murdered, did cry unto the Lord their God, for vengeance upon those which were their murderers.' Both halves of the sentence are already adjudicated in this book and within twenty-three chapters of each other: crying blood to Genesis 4:10 at Alma 14:11 ('blood crieth' is a KJV singleton), and the martyrs' demand for vengeance to Revelation 6:10 at Alma 14:26 ('avenge our blood' is a KJV singleton). Alma 37:30 fuses them, which is worth a reader's notice, but it is Alma reusing two figures the book has already given him rather than reaching for the Bible again (ADJUDICATING §4). Two further candidates were considered and declined: Luke 11:50, 'the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation', which is closest in situation and shares no distinctive wording, and Matthew 23:35, which supplies neither the crying nor the vengeance.

sharedText: never be weary of good works
reason: 'Teach them to never be weary of good works.' The New Testament says this twice — Galatians 6:9, 'let us not be weary in well doing', and 2 Thessalonians 3:13, 'be not weary in well doing' — and the sense is identical to Alma's. But 'weary in well doing' is the fixed KJV form of the idiom, occurring in those two verses and nowhere else, and Alma has neither the preposition nor the noun: 'weary OF GOOD WORKS' matches no KJV verse. Since the second half of the same clause reproduces Matthew 11:29 word for word (see the link at this verse), the failure to reproduce Paul is evidence rather than noise — the chapter can quote when it is quoting, and here it is not.

'Yea, let all thy doings be unto the Lord.' 'All thy doings' is a KJV singleton and the temptation is real, since this catalogue has already put Zephaniah 3 in Alma's hands four chapters earlier — Zephaniah 3:15 stands behind Alma 33:11. But the singleton's sense is opposed at the only point that matters. Zephaniah 3:11 reads 'In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me': the doings are sins, named as such in the same clause, and the verse is a promise that they will no longer shame the sinner. Alma's doings are the whole of a righteous young man's conduct, offered to God. The phrase in Alma is better explained as the substituted noun in the Proverbs 3:6 borrowing at 37:37 — 'in all thy doings' for Proverbs' 'in all thy ways' — where it is set up a verse in advance.

sharedText: if they would look, they might live
reason: Hardy's apparatus cross-references Numbers 21:7-9 here and the reference is sound; the link is filed four chapters earlier, at Alma 33:19, where the brazen serpent is described rather than merely alluded to — 'a type was raised up in the wilderness, that whosoever would look upon it might live' — and where Numbers 21:8's own words, looking and living, actually stand. Alma 33:20 and 33:21 are already in that link's recurrence list, and Alma 37:46 belongs with them: it is the same speaker returning to his own figure at the end of the same sermon-cycle, and it supplies no Numbers vocabulary that 33:19 does not already have. What 37:46 does add is a shift of tense and party, 'so was it with our fathers … even so it is with us. The way is prepared, and if we will look, we may live forever', which extends the type from the wilderness generation to Alma's own and from living to living forever. That extension is the verse's contribution and it is Alma's, not Moses'. See Alma 33:19 (CONVENTIONS §6a). The recurrence list at Alma 33:19 should be extended to include Alma 37:46 and Alma 37:47 when that chapter file is next touched.
